To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of the laboratory tool system with circle grid analysis is a powerful educational tool for the training of engineers in the field of sheet metal forming.

the utilization of circle grids, in conjunction with formality and simulative laboratory experiments and a simple finite element program, is an effective way to introduce students to the fundamentals and practice of sheet metal forming.

the circle grid analysis, the formability tests and the simulative tests, as presented in this chapter, provide a solid background for the education of undergraduate and graduate students of metal forming.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the experimental and numerical analysis of sheet metal forming processes.
the development and application of new technologies for sheet metal forming education.
the design of a flexible, modular and versatile laboratory tool system to support education and research in sheet metal forming.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed approach provides students with a solid background to understand the fundamentals of sheet metal forming and the practical aspects of the associated laboratory tests, which is a necessary condition to be able to design, analyze and control metal forming processes.

the proposed laboratory tool system and the associated computer program provide students and researchers with an effective and efficient tool to support the education in sheet metal forming, and to carry out basic research in sheet metal forming processes and tool systems.

this chapter presents a comprehensive and detailed description of a laboratory tool system and a computer program that are being used in conjunction to teach sheet metal forming to undergraduate and graduate students.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presented tool system and the associated computer program have been used in the last ten years in the undergraduate and graduate courses at our university to support the education in metal forming, and that they have been also used in research projects to characterize the formability and simulates the process behavior of sheet metal forming.
the presented laboratory tool system and computer program have proven their usefulness and efficiency in undergraduate and graduate courses, as well as in basic and applied research activities.

the proposed tool system and the associated computer program have been successfully applied to the teaching of undergraduate and graduate courses in sheet metal forming, as well as, to the training of engineers in industry.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a well-designed laboratory tool system, combined with a simple finite element program and a well-defined educational strategy that includes a set of laboratory tests and a set of simulative tests, can be a powerful tool to expose students to the fundamentals of sheet metal forming and the associated laboratory tests.

the utilization of the circle grid analysis in association with the laboratory tests described here provides a powerful tool to expose students to the fundamentals of sheet metal forming and to develop the necessary skills and knowledge to face the challenges of the industry.

a comprehensive and systematic use of the circle grid analysis, in conjunction with formabilty and simulative tests in sheet metal forming, provides students and researchers with the necessary background for a better understanding of the fundamentals of metal forming, the practical problems that are encountered during the design and manufacturing of sheet metal parts and the associated numerical simulation techniques.
